1001-english-and-french-communication-sk: You'll treat francophone patients and may rotate at francophone sites, so be ready to work in both languages. Language courses are possible during the program under the UGME Registration Policy.
1001-french-language-proficiency: Required before admission to the M.D.,C.M. or Med-P, as in other health programs. See the UGME Policy on Language Proficiency for accepted tests.
1001-student-campus-assignment-montreal-: You finish all studies at your assigned campus, with no transfers or changes. Med-P in Outaouais is at UQO, the M.D.,C.M. at Campus Outaouais. Electives at both are open to all.
1001-medical-equipment: Buy your own for first year: stethoscope, pen light, reflex hammer, ophthalmoscope/otoscope, 128Hz tuning forks, BP cuff, and eye protection meeting Health Canada or CSA-Z94.3.

Lab: a long white coat, an anatomy dissecting kit per two people, a box of gloves and safety glasses. Also buy two white lab jackets through UGME. The White Coat Ceremony is in September or October of second year. A phone or pager is recommended in TCP and Clerkship.
1001-registration-with-the-college-des-m: Required by law, electronically, by September 30 of first year; the CMQ emails you to confirm. Without it you can't continue.
1001-security-criminal-record-check: CMQ registration includes a record check. Training sites may ask you to declare any record. The Faculty requests withdrawal if you don't meet CMQ conditions. Some hospitals for electives ask for background checks.
1002-standards-of-behaviour-and-code-of-: You're held to professional standards even before qualifying: courtesy, respect, honesty and integrity. No harassment, abuse or mistreatment. See the Code of Conduct, Harassment Policy, Professional Behaviours, Social Media Guidelines and Medical Learner Affairs. Misconduct or a criminal conviction can mean dismissal.
1003-new-students: Register in Minerva from early June, before Orientation in mid-August. Attend Faculty Registration and Orientation in person with documents, August 18–20, 2026; missing it cancels your offer.
1003-registration-for-courses-outside-th: Language courses, or joint program courses in some cases; see the UGME registration policy.
1003-returning-students: Register in Minerva by the deadline or pay late fees. Details are emailed in early April.
1003-leaves-of-absence: Medium-term: 6 consecutive days to 7 weeks and 6 days. Long-term: 8 weeks or more. See UGME's Short-Term Absences and Medium and Long-Term Leaves policies. The program may limit their number and length.
1003-requirements-for-the-degree-of-m-d-: Meet entrance requirements and pass all evaluations. Finish within 7 years, or 8 for the M.D.,C.M. Ph.D.
1003-requirements-for-license: A degree doesn't give the right to practise; each province, state or country has its own licensing body and rules, so contact yours early. Quebec also has a French requirement (p. 70).

Regulators: Colleges of Physicians and Surgeons of Alberta (Edmonton), BC (Vancouver), Manitoba (Winnipeg), New Brunswick (Rothesay; Dr. Ed Schollenberg, Registrar), Newfoundland and Labrador (St. John's), Nova Scotia (Bedford), Ontario (Toronto), PEI (Charlottetown), Saskatchewan (Saskatoon); Collège des médecins du Québec (1250 René-Lévesque W., Office 3500).
Medical Council of Canada: 1021 Thomas Spratt Pl., Ottawa. USMLE Secretariat: 3750 Market St., Philadelphia.
1005-assessment-system: Rules can change, though usually not mid-period. Pass or fail: S or U on your transcript. Numeric grades are internal, for awards, tracking and feedback. Assessment runs by promotion period.
1005-promotion-periods: See the UGME Assessment and Promotion Policy, and older editions of the catalogue.
1005-student-promotions: This committee applies promotion rules, reviews M.D.,C.M. students and D.M.D. students during FMD, including professionalism, and has final say on suitability for medicine.
1005-failure-of-supplemental-activities: You repeat the period or are dismissed, as the committee decides. Only one repeat in the program; failing a course during it means immediate dismissal.
1005-notice-of-failures: Stay reachable; if you can't be found, you bear the consequences.
1005-curriculum-renewal-governance: The M.D.,C.M. Program Committee, chaired by the Associate Dean (UGME), designs, oversees and improves the curriculum for mission and accreditation, with students on all committees.
1005-program-overview: Courses may change; check the learning system. The current curriculum began in Fall 2013, built on "The Patient at Heart and Science in Hand": family medicine alongside science, interdisciplinary learning, and themes learned together across the years.
1006-about-the-schulich-school-of-music: Canada's largest university music school, known for orchestral, choral, opera, jazz, chamber, contemporary and early music, and for composition, theory, musicology, education, performance science, sound recording and technology.

Halls: Pollack (600), Redpath (300, with the organ), Tanna Schulich (170), Clara Lichtenstein (50). Also the Wirth Opera Studio and Multimedia Complex, with an acoustics lab, isolation booths and studios.

Marvin Duchow Music Library: 300,000+ scores, recordings, books and journals on three floors, with a unique Open Lab for recording and editing. Gertrude Whitley Performance Library: materials for 6,000+ titles.

The Applied Performance Sciences Hub researches performance, health and careers. CIRMMT is an international group on music science and technology. Labs for composition, education, recording, cognition and modelling, plus classrooms, studios and 100+ practice rooms.
About 460 undergraduates and 400 graduates; 62+ full-time and 149 part-time teachers; about 600 concerts and events a year.
1006-location: Elizabeth Wirth and Strathcona Music Buildings, 527 and 555 Sherbrooke St. W., H3A 1E3.
1006-overview-of-programs: B.Mus. and L.Mus. Music Research: Applied Performance Sciences, Composition, Education, Entrepreneurship, History, Theory, Musical Science and Technology. Performance: Conducting, Early Music, Orchestral, Piano, Voice, Organ and Guitar, Jazz. Double majors, double degrees and minors are possible across McGill. See p. 1022.
1007-music-research: The B.Mus./B.Ed. Concurrent Major (p. 1027) isn't currently offered.
1007-performance: B.Mus. takes at least three years after a Quebec DCS, or four after secondary school elsewhere.
1007-licentiate-in-music-l-mus: Three years for advanced instrumentalists and singers, focused on performance, with only basic history, theory and musicianship.
1007-minor-programs: Music minors can count as electives in a B.Mus.; minors elsewhere may also be possible. Most subjects continue to a graduate diploma, M.Mus. or M.A.
1007-music-minors-open-to-undergraduate-: Open to all bachelor's students, with home faculty approval.
1007-music-electives: Open if you meet the requirements; see the Electives site.
1007-ensembles: MUEN courses need an audition or the director's permission. Ask your home advisor if they count.
1007-scholarships-competitions-prizes-an: Entrance scholarships are automatic and renewable: Schulich, Lloyd Carr-Harris String, Student Excellence, Derek H. Davis, Suzanne Fortier (Jazz; Voice), Wirth Family (Strings; Voice), Alison Riseley Clark Organ, Mills-Tyrrell Best in the West.
Returning students' merit awards are automatic, from the year ending in April, for the next September. Competitions fund travel, projects and performance. SSAO runs other aid.
1008-summer-studies: One-month intensives, May to July; registration from early March. Up to 12 credits; over 6 in one month needs permission. Get approval before taking courses elsewhere.
1008-admission: Book a student-led tour through Discover Schulich.
1008-bachelor-of-music: Audition and record both count, and places per instrument are limited, so minimums don't guarantee entry. Non-Canadians whose first language isn't English may need TOEFL, IELTS or Duolingo before the deadline.
1008-cegep-applicants: A DEC in Music or equivalent, 75% minimum; other DECs need performance experience and may add prerequisites. Three- or four-year program.
1008-canadian-high-school-excluding-queb: A university-track diploma with 75%. Ontario: six 4U/4M courses, at least four 4U. No non-Music prerequisites. Four years.
1008-u-s-high-school-applicants: A college-track diploma with B+. No SAT or set prerequisites. Some AP credit. Four years.
1008-international-applicants: Eligible for university at home with above-average grades. IB, French Baccalaureate or three A Levels: three years. Five O Levels plus a further year: four years. Others either.
1009-transfer-students: Normally a full year of university in Good Standing, with CGPA 3.00. Non-Music credit at C or better after review; music complementary or elective credit may need more. At least 60 credits at McGill.
1009-mature-students: Age 21+, Canadian or Permanent Resident, lacking academic requirements but with exceptional talent. Send all documents; an interview may be needed.
1009-special-students: A music bachelor's or equivalent, course prerequisites and space. Usually no lessons. One year, then apply to a program.
1009-visiting-students: With prerequisites and your home university's permission.
1009-application-procedures: Music Admissions Office, 555 Sherbrooke St. W. Apply online by January 15 for September; no January entry usually. Late applications only if space remains. Recorded auditions by February 1.

Describe your background, training and intent, with diplomas or transcripts. Music Education needs a reference on teaching potential. Upload documents in the portal; official transcripts come after a decision.
1009-licentiate-in-music-l-mus-all-appli: Secondary school, music at McGill Conservatory Collegial II in Instrument or Voice and Secondary V Theory/Ear Training, plus an audition. Three years; good for those with non-music degrees or changing genres before graduate study.
1009-music-entrance-requirements: McGill Conservatory Collegial I Instrument or Voice (Performance: Collegial II) and Secondary V Theory and Ear Training.
1009-approximate-equivalents-to-entrance: CEGEP II; Toronto Conservatory, Western Board or Mount Allison Grade 9; Associated Board Grade 7. Only a guide; Performance applicants should be about two years ahead.

All must audition, on campus or by video, with equal chances. Composition: 2–3 scores, with mp3s if any, other composition work, and a one-page or 3-minute statement. Music Education: reasons in your Statement of Intent, and a reference. Upload in the portal.
1010-music-placement-examinations: New B.Mus. and L.Mus. students, and minors with prerequisites, need these for 200-level theory (MUTH, MUJZ) and musicianship (MUSP), held once a year before early June. Equivalent courses or the RCM History exam may exempt you from MUHL 186 or MUJZ 187.
1010-readmission: No Fall or Winter courses without a leave means you're inactive. Request readmission by the deadline; you may need to re-audition.
1010-tuition-fees-practical-instruction-: MUIN courses add a Music Private Lesson Fee to tuition: a term is 13 one-hour weekly lessons. Each program caps years of lessons.
One extra year of elective lessons (MUIN 110, 111) can count as electives. A second (MUIN 210, 211) needs Performance's permission and adds a post-quota Supplemental Fee.
1011-maximum-number-of-years-of-practica: Required years, all with an optional elective year. High school graduates (U0): B.Mus. Performance 4, Composition/Education/History/Theory 2, L.Mus. 3. CEGEP, transfer, IB or French Baccalaureate, and mature students (U1): Performance 3, others 1, L.Mus. 3.

Voice Coaching (MUIN 300, 301): per credit, up to two terms, for full-time Voice students, no lesson fee. Early Music and Jazz minors pay tuition plus lesson fee. Lessons aren't in Minerva: request them yearly.
1012-academic-policies-in-the-schulich-s: General requirements, requirements by program, and Academic Standing.
1012-general-academic-requirements: Be on time; grades follow the syllabus; missing exams or work without a timely valid excuse risks failure. Follow the published sequence, especially core courses, or you may lose lessons and ensembles and delay graduation.
C generally passes prerequisites; some programs need more. Keep TGPA and CGPA at 2.0 or higher.
1012-academic-requirements-by-program: These add to the general requirements.
1012-b-mus-composition: B- in all MUCO courses, or you may be advised to transfer.
1012-b-mus-performance: B- in all practical instruction, exams and ensembles. One miss gets a warning; another may mean transferring.
1012-b-mus-jazz-performance: B- in all MUJZ, MUIN and MUEN courses. A warning brings probation conditions; failing those may mean transferring.
1012-l-mus-programs: A- in all MUIN and MUEN courses. One miss gets a warning; another may mean withdrawing.
1012-academic-standing: Assessed each term, with TGPA 2.0+ expected. Fall gives Interim Satisfactory or Interim Probationary, the latter with terms for Winter. Fall decisions use only January grades, without deferred or two-term courses.
1013-satisfactory-interim-satisfactory-s: New students, CGPA 2.00+, and those meeting program requirements.
1013-probationary-interim-probationary-s: You continue under set conditions; Interim students should review loads with an advisor before add/drop.

Triggers: missing program minimum grades; TGPA or CGPA under 2.00 from Satisfactory. Staying: CGPA 1.50–1.99 and TGPA 2.50+. Readmitted from Unsatisfactory: CGPA under 2.00, meeting your letter's conditions.
1013-unsatisfactory-readmitted-standing: After readmission by the Associate Dean; your letter sets your load and conditions.
1013-unsatisfactory-interim-unsatisfacto: Interim: continue, adjusting with an advisor. Unsatisfactory after breaking probation: withdraw. Appeal to the Associate Dean by the published deadlines with proof. A second time means permanent withdrawal.
1013-incomplete-standing: No final grades yet from deferred exams (L), extensions (K) or supplementals. You may register for Fall, but it must resolve by the end of the course change period; Unsatisfactory then stops you, with appeal by proof. Still Incomplete? See Student Affairs right away.
1013-absence-policy: Attend regularly and tell your instructor about absences. No note for illness under five days; one may be asked for after five consecutive days when you miss a required task. Over 20% missed may not be accommodated. For auditions or professional work, contact Student Affairs promptly.
Make up missed learning yourself. Ask Student Affairs about missed assessments, under PASL article 7. Ensemble absences have their own policy.
1014-academic-category: Major (B.Mus., one or more); Music Studies (cross-disciplinary, with minors or outside majors); L.Mus. (shorter, performance-focused); Special (non-degree); Visiting (credit elsewhere); Exchange (official partners).
1014-accompanist-program: B.Mus. and L.Mus. students in lessons on eligible instruments can request funded hours.
1014-auditing-of-courses: No auditing for-credit courses, ensembles included, without registering. See p. 36.
1014-course-changes-and-withdrawal: Change in Minerva during add/drop. Late changes cost a fee unless the Faculty caused them, or your registration needs correcting.
Check your section for small ensembles (MUEN 560, 570, 580) before add/drop; a wrong section means a failing J.
1014-course-withdrawal: MUIN and MUEN need instructor or department approval. Others in Minerva before deadlines get a W, with no CGPA effect. Refunds depend on timing.
1014-late-course-withdrawal: Only for extenuating circumstances, requested before that term ends.
1014-distance-education-online-courses: Up to 6 elective credits. Outside courses must come from an accredited degree-granting school, count there, be approved in the Equivalency Database, and be cleared by Student Affairs first.
1015-electives: Non-music, music and free. See the Electives site.
1015-music-electives: Any non-required Music course may count as free or music elective. Extra ensembles can count as complementary performance or electives.
1015-non-music-electives: Undergraduate courses from other faculties, like French or computer science. Extras become free electives. One a term may be S/U.
1015-free-electives: Any mix of music and non-music.
1015-schulich-school-of-music-ensemble-p: Ensembles train practical musicianship throughout. Small: usually 1 credit (MUEN 540, 541, 571 are 0.5), for Performance majors, L.Mus. and Jazz and Early Music minors. Large: 2 credits, for all B.Mus. and L.Mus. Check your program; extras need approval.

Orchestral instruments: flute, oboe, clarinet, bassoon, saxophone, French horn, trumpet, trombone, tuba, percussion, harp, violin, viola, cello, double bass. Voice majors use vocal and choral ensembles. "Director" includes conductor, stage director and coach. Rules apply to everyone in any ensemble.
1015-small-ensembles: MUEN 540, 541, 567, 569 and 571 don't meet small ensemble requirements, but can be complementary or electives. See the Ensemble or Jazz Combo sites.
1016-large-ensembles: New violin, viola or cello students in orchestral programs take MUEN 565 in Fall and Winter of first year. See Ensemble Auditions.
1016-ensemble-assignments-and-auditions: Large ensembles need an audition; for small ones, ask the director. If you can't attend, tell the supervisor two weeks ahead in writing and send a recording; otherwise the department assigns you. You're told by email before rehearsals start.
Assignments may change; ask how it affects grades. Orchestral, piano, guitar or percussion students without a place may take choir or ask the Ensemble Office.
1016-commitment: Ensembles are courses: attend all rehearsals, concerts, trips and recordings. You get notice of extra rehearsals, which are avoided if possible.
1016-request-to-be-excused-from-a-rehear: Applies to large ensembles and MUEN 567. Tell ensembles.music@mcgill.ca of professional engagements before placement. Fill out an Absence Request Form as soon as you know. Orchestral: find your own substitute.

Maximum four absences a term (two per orchestral cycle), excused or not, and none for dress rehearsals or concerts. More keeps you out of that cycle; for illness, ask about reassignment, extra work or late withdrawal. If hurt, attend and take notes. See Student Accessibility and Achievement if needed.
Penalties without approval: up to 10 minutes late, or arriving during tuning, drops one grade point (B to B-). Absent or later drops a full letter (A to B).

Valid reasons, not guaranteed: illness, medical or dental work (email before, form within 3 days of returning); audition, master class, major competition, important engagement, family emergency or occasion, other field trip, McGill function, religious observance (email a day before, form in advance and within 48 hours). Report pain to your teacher and director, and don't perform with injury.
1017-preparation: If unprepared, the director warns you in writing through the supervisor and coordinator. After that you can be removed from a performance. Withdrawing for this gives an F.
1018-withdrawal-from-an-ensemble: Needs the Ensemble Office, Director or Student Affairs, and you make up the credits later.
1018-failing-an-ensemble: Academic probation and making up the credit. Failing the same one again may mean withdrawing.
1018-exemption-from-a-required-ensemble-: For a major competition or significant voice role after minimum terms, with teacher, coordinator and director approval; or when only your final exam remains; or only non-music or free electives remain; or a significant medical reason. This doesn't satisfy credits.
1018-rotation-in-large-ensembles: Seating may rotate for fairness, as director and coordinators decide.
1018-performance-library: You pay for lost or damaged music, and Minerva holds can follow.
1018-examinations-deferrals-and-rereads: Governed by PASL. Talk to your instructor first.
1018-practical-examinations: Held in official exam periods. Final-year students finishing in Summer may request early September (MUIN 283, 482, 452), recorded as Summer, through practicalexams.music@mcgill.ca. Otherwise plan for December or April.
1019-practical-examination-marking: The mark averages all examiners, and at least half must pass you to advance. Minimums: L.Mus. A- (80%), B.Mus. Performance B- (65%), Concentration and performance minors C (55%). If the average passes but most fail you, you get the grade just below the minimum.
Decide readiness with your teacher, choose material, and apply on the form, as exams aren't in Minerva. Late applications cost $50, with permission.
Application / cancellation: December, October 15 / November 15. April, February 15 / March 15. Early September, May 31 / August 1. Cancel free until then. Email to cancel or defer.
1019-deferrals: Talk to an advisor first. Final exams: apply in Minerva; write in the deferred period; missing it gets a failing J.

Practical exams and recitals: only for serious illness or unforeseen events, not travel or colds. Apply in Minerva and email within 24 hours. December moves to next April, April to December. You get an L until done. No second deferrals; withdrawal only in exceptional cases.
1020-assessment-task-extensions: Ask your instructor before the deadline (PASL article 7). Past term's end you get a K and finish by an agreed date next term.
1020-rereads-for-graded-assessments-and-: You can see and discuss marked work (PASL). Review with your instructor, then request a third-party reread, done by an impartial academic. The grade can go up or down and stands. Ask Student Affairs for deadlines.
1020-graduation-requirements: Complete all requirements for each program; C or higher in required and prerequisite courses, D only in other electives; CGPA 2.00. Residency: 60 credits for B.Mus., 48 for L.Mus. Apply to graduate.
1020-graduation-honours: Dean's Honour List, Distinction, and Outstanding Achievement for superior performance or scholarship.
1020-incomplete-grades: K is at the instructor's discretion, due within four months; then KF (failed), or KE if extended. Ks don't count toward in-course scholarships. Abandoning a course without withdrawing gets a failing J. In exceptional cases, the Associate Dean may allow KK, permanently incomplete and outside your GPA.
